What Does a Harness Repair?
A Preregistered Study of Visibility, Baseline Adequacy and Evaluation Defects

Bowen Xu* bxu666@stanford.eduDepartment of Biology, Stanford University, Stanford, CA, USA    Boyu Chen*Institute of Health Informatics, University College London, London, UK    *Equal contribution. Corresponding author
Abstract

Harness search keeps a change to the prompts, reasoning switches, token budgets or parsers around a frozen model if the change raises a score. Such a gain can come from answers the parser could not read before, a weak comparison, or a defect in the evaluation. We preregistered a study of where these gains come from, with three small models, three benchmarks, replication and test partitions, a GEPA search arm and six evaluation defects injected one at a time, and we report all 47 primary endpoints. Turning thinking off raised accuracy over a capped thinking setting in 5 of 9 model-benchmark cells, and in each the gain came mostly from questions where the capped setting gave no readable answer. The thinking-off setting was not meaningfully worse than a rescue configuration or four GEPA-selected harnesses in 11 of 13 comparisons, and lost to the rescue on GSM8K for two models. GEPA repaired its broken starting points, but none of its selected harnesses was more accurate than the thinking-off setting. A thinking budget in the serving engine, which also allows a longer answer, lowered truncation and raised the parse rate in 6 of 9 cells. In 6 of 15 evaluable defect-model pairs, replication through the same pipeline reproduced the defect’s distortion instead of revealing it. On the LongevityBench multiple-choice tasks, only the longevity-tuned model beat the strongest constant-label baseline.

1 Introduction

A harness is everything around a frozen model that changes what it is scored on: the prompts, reasoning switches, token budgets, retry rules and parsers. Harness search proposes a change and keeps it if it wins (Agrawal et al., 2025; Khattab et al., 2023; Wu et al., 2026; Lee et al., 2026b). A gain that replicates on untouched rows shows that the selected harness beat its parent by more than selection noise, and it leaves three questions open. The first is visibility versus quality: did the answers get better, or did answers that the parent never produced in a readable form, because it ran out of tokens or never committed to one, become visible to the parser? The second is baseline adequacy: would a simple setting that the search never tried do as well, and does the model beat trivial baselines at all? The third is evaluation validity: are the inputs, the gold labels, the split and the served model what they are said to be?

Each question has a literature (Section 2), and most of it works after the fact. Harness and scaffold gains vanish against matched-budget test-time scaling and simple baselines (Wang et al., 2026b; Gideoni et al., 2026; Liang et al., 2026; Kapoor et al., 2024), a gain can be completion rather than correctness (Seyoum & Mittur, 2026; Lee, 2026; Chen et al., 2026), thinking off can beat a thinking cap (Nie et al., 2026), and evaluation pipelines carry defects that move scores by tens of points (Zhu et al., 2025; Berriche et al., 2026). We found no study that fixes in advance, for a stated contrast, how much of a harness gain is visibility, none that tests the benchmark authors’ own protocol against searched harnesses with a margin, and none that injects known defects one at a time to ask whether replication reproduces them. The search covered 2024-01 to 2026-10-03 and was capped at 200 web searches, and three of its six parts had to be resumed after a rate limit, so these statements are bounded (Appendix H).

Background.

This study follows a case study of harness search around a frozen longevity language model (Appendix A). Its search scored every candidate through a caller that sent each benchmark row’s reference answer to the model as an earlier assistant turn, and the rescue it selected replicated on a second shard through the same caller, so replication could not detect the defect: every call carried it. Trivial baselines, input audits and per-call prompt-token reconciliation did. After the caller was corrected, a preregistered re-evaluation found that the search’s starting configuration parsed none of its 556 prospective rows, and that a thinking-off setting the search had never tried was non-inferior to the rescue at less than half the token cost. This paper asks whether that one model, one benchmark and one defect is a pattern.

This paper.

We preregistered a study of what a harness repairs and froze it on 30 September 2026 at 06:53:11 UTC. It uses three small models, three benchmark pools, a replication partition and a confirmatory test partition, an adaptive arm in which GEPA (Agrawal et al., 2025) searches for harnesses, and six evaluation defects that we inject one at a time. We split the gain of a thinking-off protocol over a capped thinking configuration exactly into rows only the protocol parses, rows both parse, and rows only the capped configuration parses, the split that Chen et al. (2026) use for self-revision, and we fix a dominance statistic and a gain gate in advance. We test the thinking-off protocol for non-inferiority against a derived rescue and four GEPA-selected harnesses, with trivial baselines next to every accuracy, and we test whether the serving stack’s thinking budget, which also allows a longer answer, lowers truncation. For each defect and model we fix one claim in advance, that replication through the same pipeline confirms the defect’s distortion, and we measure the false alarms of five audit checks. All 47 primary endpoints, in four families, are reported with every deviation and addendum, and everything computed after the outputs existed is labelled.

The results cover three small models, three pools and six defects, and nothing beyond them. We do not claim that harness gains can be illusory, that thinking off can beat a thinking cap, or that agent and harness evaluations can be preregistered, since each has been shown or done before, and we do not claim that harness search finds genuine quality gains.

2 Related work

We organise related work by the questions of Section 1; Appendix H states how it was searched and what the search could not cover.

Harness search, and whether its gains are real.

Prompt optimisers (Zhou et al., 2023; Yang et al., 2024; Khattab et al., 2023; Agrawal et al., 2025) and harness search (Lee et al., 2026b; Wu et al., 2026; Zhang et al., 2025) treat the text and control flow around fixed weights as the object of search, and GEPA is the adaptive arm of our study. Earlier work has shown, after the fact, that such gains can be illusory: evolved harnesses and scaffolds do not beat matched-budget test-time scaling or simple baselines (Wang et al., 2026b; Gideoni et al., 2026; Liang et al., 2026; Kapoor et al., 2024), a hardware-verification harness gains mostly completion (Seyoum & Mittur, 2026), a search started from a defective seed fails (Liu et al., 2026), and self-improving loops tamper with or hack their evaluators (Wang et al., 2026a; Yang et al., 2026a). Our question is narrower: where the gain of one protocol comes from, and whether a known defect would be seen, with the questions and decision rules fixed in advance.

Visibility and quality (H1).

Chen et al. (2026) split the accuracy change of a self-revision step into a content margin, a format-recovery margin, a format-loss margin and a dead cell, which is our split under other names but without a predefined dominance threshold. Nie et al. (2026) and Kaiser et al. (2026) give the identity for a single configuration or between models, completion rate times conditional accuracy; under a shared budget thinking off beats capped thinking (Nie et al., 2026; Ma et al., 2025), and capped single-call evaluation of hybrid models has been called an artifact of protocol (Lee et al., 2026a). Other work finds that unparsed answers hide correct ones (Garware & Zisad, 2026), separates traces cut by a cap from traces that finished without an answer (Goyal & Ray, 2026), reads a harness-evolution gain informally as completion rather than correctness on the twelve tasks that had been searched (Seyoum & Mittur, 2026), and counts repaired abstentions for constrained decoding (Lee, 2026). We add a pre-specified dominance statistic and gain gate, applied prospectively to the contrast between a thinking-off protocol and a capped thinking configuration.

Baseline adequacy (H2).

Several studies find, after the fact, that simple baselines match searched or evolved harnesses and complex agents (Kapoor et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2026b; Gideoni et al., 2026; Liang et al., 2026; Chang & Chen, 2026). A preregistered non-inferiority test of a simple alternative exists for agent memory (Sharma & Lall, 2026), and equivalence margins have been used for scaffolds (Gringras, 2026) and for compression (Singh, 2026). Our test fixes the margin in advance for the benchmark authors’ own protocol, against a derived rescue and four GEPA-selected harnesses.

Budget forcing (H3).

Budget forcing and the Qwen3 thinking budget (Muennighoff et al., 2025; Yang et al., 2025) serve as evaluation controls, with a forced answer or a forced end of thinking (Nie et al., 2026; Carlon et al., 2026; Lee et al., 2026a; Chang & Chen, 2026), and one study forces the answer delimiter at a cap in vLLM (Goyal & Ray, 2026). We test the engine’s thinking-token budget (Kwon et al., 2023) as a harness setting against a capped configuration; the technique is not ours.

Defects and prospective replication (H4).

Other work injects faults with known ground truth and measures false alarms: tool bugs in agent benchmarks (Bellibatlu et al., 2026), tampering edits (Wang et al., 2026a), reward-hacking channels (Yang et al., 2026a) and planted gains (Shawn, 2026). Defects like ours have been catalogued as they occurred, for answer-key access, label defaults, parser fallbacks, stop sequences, denominators and gold errors (Wahi, 2026; Berriche et al., 2026; Zhu et al., 2025), and the reference scorer of MMLU-Pro credits a random option for an empty prediction.11 1 evaluate_from_local.py, function save_res, in the repository TIGER-AI-Lab/MMLU-Pro, read on 2026-10-03. We found no study that injects pipeline defects one at a time into a harness-search pipeline and tests, for each defect and model, whether replication through the same pipeline reproduces the distortion.

Served-model identity and determinism.

Serving stacks change outputs at fixed weights (Pape et al., 2026; Wang, 2026; Yuan et al., 2025; He & Thinking Machines Lab, 2025), answers can flip while accuracy stays flat (Dutta et al., 2024; Kübler et al., 2026), and a served route is not its model identifier (Stenstrom et al., 2026; Gao et al., 2025). vLLM used to decide tying from the configuration alone and silently discarded a stored head; its fix (hmellor (2026), vLLM project) is in the version we used (vLLM 0.30.0), which loads the stored head. We add a measured instance of the mismatch, since the mechanism is known.

GEPA from a broken start.

Liu et al. (2026) report that GEPA, started from its official GSM8K seed (which puts the answer before the reasoning), falls from 23.81% to 13.50% and never repairs the order, and Ursekar et al. (2026) start optimisers from deliberately untuned seeds, one of them a non-functional stub. Ours is a controlled comparison of clean and broken starts; why a search repairs one defect and not another is not tested here.

Preregistration and prospective design.

Preregistered or frozen designs with deviation logs, holdouts or equivalence margins appear in Gringras (2026); Weinberger & Hozez (2026); Sharma & Lall (2026); Lee (2026); Goyal & Ray (2026); Liang et al. (2026); Bellibatlu et al. (2026); Singh (2026). Thomas et al. (2026) confirm on the first eligible model released after the plan, a stronger standard than ours, since our freeze guards the rules and not model-specific tuning. We found no earlier study that combines the freeze with its hash and time in the commit, a pilot, replication then test, an adaptive arm before replication, all 47 endpoints reported, addenda that state what had been seen, and an exposure log.

3 Design

The design is the frozen preregistration (hash and time in Appendix E), and this section states only what the results need.

3.1 Setting

Models and stack.

We study Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity (Zhavoronkov et al., 2026), a Qwen3 (Yang et al., 2025) model tuned on aging-biology data, SmolLM3-3B (Bakouch et al., 2025) and Intern-S1-mini (Bai et al., 2025), on vLLM 0.30.0 (Kwon et al., 2023) in batch-invariant mode (He & Thinking Machines Lab, 2025) at zero temperature and client concurrency 32, on one RTX 5090. The Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity checkpoint declares tied embeddings but stores a different output matrix, and the study model uses the stored one (untied); the tied variant that the case study served returns only in the FreeToken (Yang et al., 2026b) continuity runs for the tied-output-layer defect. Two models also have a descriptive seeded-sampling arm.

Pools, cells and partitions.

The LongevityBench letter pool combines, by row, LB-0030 (age band, five options), LB-0034 (which of two participants is older) and LB-0042 (ten-year survival), and LB-0038, an age regression, is reported apart. MMLU-Pro (Wang et al., 2024) (a stratified subset of 2,000 items) and GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021) are the other two pools, and a cell is a model with a pool, so there are nine cells. The items are split into search, replication and test partitions (40/20/40); LongevityBench’s 14,720 rows, in 2,104 participant components, are split by component so that no participant spans partitions, and GEPA searches on the search partition only. The analysis rows leave out 147 replication and 371 test rows that the case study had held out and later called, and 7 replication rows whose reference answers could be recovered from an upload made by mistake; putting them back is a sensitivity analysis. The test cells then have 3,942 letter rows (789 participant components, the bootstrap unit), 799 MMLU-Pro items and 527 GSM8K items, and the replication cells have 1,990, 399 and 264.

3.2 Configurations and scoring

Table 1 lists the six configurations of the grid and the GEPA harnesses. A call is unparsed if the scorer cannot read an answer from it, and it then scores as wrong, so an unparsed answer may hide a correct answer, a wrong one or none. A call is truncated if it ended at the token limit (finish reason length), whatever the scorer makes of it, and non-committed if it ended by itself (finish reason stop) and is unparsed; for RESCUE-1500 both properties are those of the call that gives the answer.

For H1, let P be the baseline configuration and R the comparison, paired on the nn rows of a cell, with uu the parse indicator and cc the correct indicator of a call and a bar negating an indicator. Row ii is in V if only R parses it (u¯P,i​uR,i\bar{u}_{P,i}u_{R,i}), in B if both parse it (uP,i​uR,iu_{P,i}u_{R,i}) and in L if only P parses it (uP,i​u¯R,iu_{P,i}\bar{u}_{R,i}). With Δ=∑i(cR,i−cP,i)/n\Delta=\sum_{i}(c_{R,i}-c_{P,i})/n and the contributions ΔV=∑iVi​cR,i/n\Delta_{V}=\sum_{i}V_{i}c_{R,i}/n (P scores zero on V), ΔB=∑iBi​(cR,i−cP,i)/n\Delta_{B}=\sum_{i}B_{i}(c_{R,i}-c_{P,i})/n and ΔL=−∑iLicP,i/n\Delta_{L}=-\sum_{i}L_{i}c_{P,i}/n, the identity Δ=ΔV+ΔB+ΔL\Delta=\Delta_{V}+\Delta_{B}+\Delta_{L} is exact, because a row that neither configuration parses adds nothing. Each contribution is divided by the cell’s nn and not by the size of its row set, as in the tables, so ΔV\Delta_{V} is R’s number of correct answers on V per row of the cell. Chen et al. (2026) use this additive split for self-revision (content, format-recovery and format-loss margins); the dominance statistic, its fixed share and the gain gate are ours. The dominance statistic T=ΔV−0.8​(ΔV+ΔB)T=\Delta_{V}-0.8\,(\Delta_{V}+\Delta_{B}) is positive when visibility supplies more than 0.8 of what the rows R parses contribute.

3.3 Hypotheses and endpoints

Table 2 states the four hypotheses. Their 47 primary endpoints are the only confirmatory results, and their verdicts come from percentile-bootstrap intervals adjusted within each family.

3.4 Defects, claims and checks (H4)

Six defects arose in the case study, and we inject each into a harness-search pipeline, one at a time, and compare the result with the clean pipeline on the same rows. The pipeline’s start ss is THINK-1536, and the reported quantity is the start’s accuracy on the letter pool, measured on a selection sample SS (the replication partition) and on a check sample RR (the test partition); for the broken start it is the gain over the start. Let DSD_{S} and DRD_{R} be a defect’s distortion of the reported quantity on SS and on RR, and Γ=DR−DS\Gamma=D_{R}-D_{S}. The reference-answer defect (A) sends the row’s reference answer as an assistant turn, on 1,204 replication rows halved by component into SS and RR. The gold fallback (B1) takes LB-0042’s gold from a historical fallback that, with this release’s labels, differs from the derived gold on about half of its rows, and the unparsed-as-A scoring (B2) scores an unparsed answer as the letter A. The skewed split (C) re-implements the case study’s split, with SS and RR the halves of its validation part. The broken start (D) starts from THINK-64 and reports the gain of the selected configuration over the start; the selection does not depend on the start, so it cancels, and the distortion is DS=accS​(THINK-1536)−accS​(THINK-64)D_{S}=\mathrm{acc}_{S}(\text{\mbox{{\small THINK-1536}}})-\mathrm{acc}_{S}(\text{\mbox{{\small THINK-64}}}), with the same difference on RR for DRD_{R}. The tied output layer (E) serves the tied layer in place of the untied one (Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity only), as an engine that decides tying from the configuration alone does (hmellor (2026), vLLM project). Appendix I gives each defect’s construction, clean counterpart, samples and evaluability bound, and each check’s predicate and threshold.

The claim for a defect and a model holds if DSD_{S} and DRD_{R} lie wholly outside ±m\pm m with the same sign and Γ\Gamma lies wholly inside ±m\pm m; it fails if any of the three lies wholly on the other side of its boundary, and it is inconclusive otherwise. A pair is evaluable only if the largest distortion its mechanism can cause on SS exceeds mm, a bound that we compute from parse, gold-change and answer-difference indicators without accuracy; the skewed split changes the sample and has no row-level bound, so it is evaluable by rule. The family stays at 16 whatever is evaluable. Five checks read the defects’ signatures: per-call prompt-token reconciliation (TR), trivial baselines (TB), the simple configuration family (SCF), input reading (IR) and the gain and level rules of prospective replication (PR), plus served-model identity (SMI) for the tied output layer. Their detection matrix is largely true by construction and descriptive, and what is empirical is their false alarms on clean pipelines.

3.5 Statistics and what was fixed in advance

Every contrast is paired on rows. In each of B=50,000B=50{,}000 bootstrap resamples we draw the cell’s units with replacement (participant components for LongevityBench, items for MMLU-Pro and GSM8K), so that a unit drawn kk times counts its rows kk times; every statistic of the cell is recomputed on the resample with each row weighted by the draw of its unit, and all contrasts of a cell share the resample. The seed of a cell derives from a hash of its partition, model and pool (base 4242). The BB statistics are sorted ascending and indexed from zero, and for a two-sided tail probability qq the lower bound of the interval is the value at index ⌊B​q⌋−1\lfloor Bq\rfloor-1 and the upper bound the value at index ⌈B⁡(1−q)⌉−1\lceil B(1-q)\rceil-1, clamped to the range of indices. Every estimate carries an unadjusted 95% interval (q=0.025q=0.025), and a verdict uses the Bonferroni-adjusted interval of its family, with q=0.025/mq=0.025/m for mm endpoints (levels 99.44%, 99.62%, 99.44% and 99.69% for H1–H4). These levels are nominal: a percentile bootstrap covers only approximately, so the family-wise error rate is controlled approximately and is not guaranteed. For H4, the resample of an instance’s units also serves its clean counterpart where the two share their rows (all defects except the skewed split, which uses other rows and is resampled independently), so that DSD_{S} and DRD_{R} are paired, and Γ\Gamma pairs the bb-th resample of SS with the bb-th of RR, which are disjoint samples drawn with their own seeds. A test verdict is replicated if the replication partition gives the same verdict, not replicated if it gives the opposite one, and inconclusive replication otherwise. The error control of H4 covers “holds” only, and “fails” is a descriptive label. The preregistration was frozen at 06:53:11 UTC on 30 September 2026, before any replication or test item was called, and the pilot called 700 pilot items only. The directions of H1 and H3 were visible in the pilot’s parse and truncation rates, and the primary set of H1 changed twice before the freeze after those rates were seen (Section 5).

4 Results

Results are on the test partition, the confirmatory one, unless stated, and the replication partition enters through the replication label. Primary endpoints carry the family-adjusted interval and everything else the unadjusted 95% interval; Appendix B gives every endpoint in full.

4.1 The 47 primary endpoints at a glance

Table 3 gives the 31 endpoints of H1–H3 and Table 4 the 16 pairs of H4, and the sections below take them in turn. Of the 31 endpoints of H1–H3, 30 are replicated and 1 is an inconclusive replication, and the number labelled not replicated is 0. Figure 1 plots the adjusted intervals.

4.2 H1: visibility dominates where the thinking cap truncates

Visibility dominates in SmolLM3-3B on all three pools and in Intern-S1-mini on the letters and MMLU-Pro. In these five cells AUTHORS-1500 gains over THINK-512 between Δ=+0.060\Delta=+0.060 [+0.046+0.046, +0.074+0.074] (SmolLM3-3B, letters) and +0.403+0.403 [+0.352+0.352, +0.456+0.456] (Intern-S1-mini, MMLU-Pro), and the gain is visibility: ΔV\Delta_{V} is at least Δ\Delta in all five (shares from 1.00 to 1.82), because the rows both configurations parse contribute at most ΔB≤+0.001\Delta_{B}\leq+0.001 and the rows only THINK-512 parses cost ΔL\Delta_{L} (for SmolLM3-3B on GSM8K, ΔV=+0.197\Delta_{V}=+0.197, ΔB=−0.036\Delta_{B}=-0.036 and ΔL=−0.053\Delta_{L}=-0.053). Almost all of THINK-512’s unparsed calls ended at the token limit; the exception is SmolLM3-3B on the letters, where 543 of 3,394 ended by themselves without an answer (non-committed). Two of the five verdicts are nearly settled by construction, as the preregistration expected for the first. In Intern-S1-mini on the letters both configurations parse only 1 row of 3,942, so ΔB\Delta_{B} is nearly zero and TT, nearly a fifth of ΔV\Delta_{V}, is positive (the preregistration listed the cell as “T>0T>0 nearly inevitable”). In Intern-S1-mini on MMLU-Pro, B has 69 of 799 rows, so ΔB\Delta_{B} cannot exceed that share, which is below a quarter of the observed ΔV=+0.419\Delta_{V}=+0.419, and T>0T>0 follows from B’s row count and that observed ΔV\Delta_{V}. The verdict is informative in SmolLM3-3B’s three cells, where B has 448, 81 and 340 rows.

The other four cells fail the gain gate. Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity needs no visibility, since THINK-512 parses 1.000 of the letter rows, 0.940 of MMLU-Pro and 0.992 of GSM8K, and Δ=−0.003\Delta=-0.003 [−0.018-0.018, +0.012+0.012] on the letters. In Intern-S1-mini on GSM8K the gate fails the other way, because AUTHORS-1500 loses accuracy (Δ=−0.287\Delta=-0.287 [−0.355-0.355, −0.218-0.218]); there T=+0.286T=+0.286 is positive only because ΔB=−0.343\Delta_{B}=-0.343 is large and negative, the reading the gate exists to stop, and THINK-512 is the more accurate configuration on the rows both parse. The sanity checks (THINK-64 against AUTHORS-1500) give visibility dominates in 8 of nine cells, as expected, and fail the gate where Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity already parses GSM8K.

4.3 H2: the thinking-off baseline is non-inferior in most cells and fails on GSM8K for two models

AUTHORS-1500 is non-inferior to RESCUE-1500 in 7 of nine cells and to all four GEPA harnesses. It fails on GSM8K for SmolLM3-3B (θ=−0.089\theta=-0.089 [−0.129-0.129, −0.053-0.053]) and for Intern-S1-mini (θ=−0.342\theta=-0.342 [−0.402-0.402, −0.281-0.281]), where the rescue is more accurate than the thinking-off configuration by more than the margin. The study does not isolate which part of the rescue, the thinking within 512 tokens or the second call, accounts for the difference. We expected the Intern-S1-mini endpoint to be inconclusive, an informal expectation from a planned adjusted power of 0.19 at a true θ\theta of zero (Appendix K), and it is not close. For SmolLM3-3B on GSM8K the replication partition is inconclusive, so the label is an inconclusive replication. In Intern-S1-mini’s letter cell the rescue equals AUTHORS-1500 (θ=0.000\theta=0.000, since every THINK-512 call is cut off), so holds is trivial there.

GEPA searched prompt text only (Appendix J), repaired its broken starts, and found no harness whose accuracy differs detectably from the thinking-off baseline’s. In the clean-start run with seed zero no proposal beat the seed on the validation rows, so its selected harness is the seed, AUTHORS-1500 itself (θ=0.000\theta=0.000 by construction). The other three selected harnesses parse every test row and reach accuracy 0.620 to 0.631, against 0.632 for AUTHORS-1500; θ\theta runs from +0.002+0.002 to +0.012+0.012, and all three adjusted intervals contain zero. Their validation scores (0.660 to 0.700 over the four runs) exceed their test accuracy in every run, as selection makes them optimistic, and none of the candidates GEPA saw (192 to 377 per run) contained a soft switch (/think or /no_think).

4.4 H3: BUDGET-512-1500 lowers truncation where THINK-512 truncates

BUDGET-512-1500 lowers truncation and raises parsing in the six cells where THINK-512 truncates a large share, with DTD_{T} from +0.260+0.260 (SmolLM3-3B, GSM8K) to +0.979+0.979 (Intern-S1-mini, letters), DPD_{P} from +0.151+0.151 to +0.662+0.662, and both adjusted lower bounds above the minimal difference. In the Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity letter and GSM8K cells THINK-512 does not truncate (adjusted upper bounds +0.001+0.001 and 0.0000.000), so there is no room for a drop of 0.05. In Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity on MMLU-Pro DT=DP=+0.060D_{T}=D_{P}=+0.060 with adjusted interval [+0.038+0.038, +0.085+0.085], which contains 0.05, so the verdict is inconclusive. The parse gain is not the whole story for SmolLM3-3B: after the forced end of thinking it re-opens a turn in 4,384 of its 7,216 test calls, and BUDGET-512-1500 still ends by itself without an answer on 0.424 of its letter rows.

What H3 isolates.

BUDGET-512-1500 differs from THINK-512 in two ways at once: vLLM ends thinking after 512 tokens, and the total allowance is 2,012 tokens against 512. H3 therefore supports the combined change and not forced termination alone. As a partial and descriptive comparison, THINK-1536, with an allowance of 1,536 tokens and no forcing, still ends at the token limit in 0.066 (SmolLM3-3B, GSM8K) to 0.800 (Intern-S1-mini, letters) of its calls in the six cells where THINK-512 truncates a large share, against 0.021 to 0.379 for BUDGET-512-1500, which truncates less in all six. The two differ in allowance as well (2,012 against 1,536 tokens), so the comparison does not separate forcing from allowance.

Is the truncation an artifact of zero temperature?

In the two models with a seeded arm, substantial truncation persists under sampling (descriptive; Table 22). Sampling at the model cards’ recommended values (Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity: temperature 0.6, top-pp 0.95, top-kk 20; Intern-S1-mini: 0.8, 1.0, 50), with a seed per request, changes THINK-512’s truncation by at most 0.023 in ten of the 12 cells (two models, three pools, two partitions) and raises it for Intern-S1-mini on GSM8K by +0.097+0.097 (test) and +0.098+0.098 (replication). Under sampling THINK-512 still ends at the token limit in 0.619 to 0.997 of Intern-S1-mini’s test calls, and the drop in truncation that H3 measures, recomputed on the seeded outputs with unadjusted intervals, runs from +0.581+0.581 to +0.963+0.963 for Intern-S1-mini and is +0.068+0.068 for Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity on MMLU-Pro, next to +0.060+0.060 with greedy decoding. The preregistered verdicts use family-adjusted intervals at another level, so the seeded statistics are not compared with them, and SmolLM3-3B has no seeded arm.

4.5 H4: prospective replication confirms the distortion in six of fifteen pairs

The claim holds in six pairs: the broken start in all three models, the unparsed-as-A scoring in SmolLM3-3B and Intern-S1-mini, and the gold fallback in Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity. Under the broken start the reported gain over the start is inflated by DS=+0.638D_{S}=+0.638, +0.164+0.164 and +0.124+0.124 (Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity, SmolLM3-3B, Intern-S1-mini) and by almost the same amount on RR (Γ=−0.003\Gamma=-0.003, −0.007-0.007, +0.001+0.001). Scoring unparsed answers as A inflates the start’s accuracy by +0.208+0.208 and +0.289+0.289, exactly the share the start leaves unparsed with gold A, and the gold fallback moves Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity’s start by −0.145-0.145. In all six the distortion is large and reappears on RR, so a replication would have reproduced the distorted report instead of revealing it.

The claim fails in four pairs: the gold fallback in SmolLM3-3B and Intern-S1-mini, whose starts parse too few of the rows whose gold the fallback changes (bounds 0.083 and 0.057, distortions +0.001+0.001 and −0.012-0.012); the skewed split in SmolLM3-3B; and the tied output layer in Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity, where DS=+0.005D_{S}=+0.005 and DR=+0.014D_{R}=+0.014 both lie inside the band. Five pairs are inconclusive, the reference-answer defect in all three models and the skewed split in Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity and Intern-S1-mini; for the reference-answer defect in Intern-S1-mini both DS=+0.142D_{S}=+0.142 and DR=+0.164D_{R}=+0.164 clear the band, but the interval of Γ\Gamma, [−0.065-0.065, +0.108+0.108], is wide because each half has only 81 components. The unparsed-as-A scoring in Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity is not evaluable, because its start leaves no row unparsed (bound 0.000). These counts follow the general rule of the preregistration for DRD_{R}, which the pinned code implements (Section 5); under the narrower reading that grades only the two sub-cases listed after the general rule, the skewed split in SmolLM3-3B is inconclusive and the counts are 6 holds, 3 fails and 6 inconclusive (Appendix C).

The audit checks.

Table 5 summarises the six checks of Section 3.4. Their detection matrix is descriptive and largely true by construction: every rule expected to fire did so in 12 of the 16 instances (Appendices D and B give the exceptions and each instance). What is empirical is the false alarms on the clean instances: IR4 fires on 7 of 7, SCF1 on 4, SCF2 on 4, TB2 on 3, SCF3 on 2 and the gain rule of PR on 1, and no other rule fires on a clean instance.

4.6 Descriptive results

Accuracy next to the trivial baselines.

Table 6 gives the accuracy of five configurations in the three pools next to their baselines, computed after the outputs existed (Appendix C), with a block for each LongevityBench task; THINK-64, the GEPA harnesses and the replication partition are in Appendix B. Each oracle constant is chosen once, on the analysis rows of the partition it is scored on, and it is a fixed prediction in the bootstrap: it is not re-chosen in a resample, so the intervals of the differences to it cover the sampling of units given that choice. On the LongevityBench letters the strongest constant is the oracle constant label: the age band most common on LB-0030, Participant A on LB-0034 and “Yes” on LB-0042 (0.840 of its test rows). It scores 0.539 [0.527, 0.551] on the pool, far above chance (0.380) and the oracle constant letter (0.389), because the option order is shuffled (120 letter-to-label mappings on LB-0030, 2 on LB-0042) and a constant letter cannot exploit an uneven label distribution. Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity exceeds the strongest constant in every configuration that parses: AUTHORS-1500 0.632, +0.093+0.093 [+0.074+0.074, +0.112+0.112], and THINK-512 +0.096+0.096 [+0.077+0.077, +0.115+0.115]. The margin is small on LB-0042 (+0.027+0.027 [+0.007+0.007, +0.048+0.048] for THINK-512), where one GEPA harness, GEPA-CLEAN-s1, is not above it (−0.010-0.010 [−0.034-0.034, +0.015+0.015]). SmolLM3-3B and Intern-S1-mini are below the strongest constant on the pool in every configuration (at best −0.382-0.382 and −0.225-0.225), because most of their calls end unparsed and unparsed counts as wrong, although Intern-S1-mini is above it on LB-0034 with AUTHORS-1500 (+0.060+0.060 [+0.003+0.003, +0.117+0.117]).

The case study had not found this: on the split of its harness search no configuration of the same model clearly exceeded a constant age band on LB-0030 or the majority letter on LB-0034 (post hoc there). We read the difference as consistent with that split’s skew toward young, alive participants, but the items, the output layer (tied there, untied here) and the stack all differ, so the data do not establish it. The output layer alone is unlikely to explain it: on the same items the tied and untied variants differ in accuracy by at most 0.009, although their parsed answers are identical on only 0.656 to 0.741 of the rows, and on the letter pool the tied-output-layer defect moves the start’s accuracy by DS=+0.005D_{S}=+0.005 and DR=+0.014D_{R}=+0.014, inside the band.

The general pools.

On MMLU-Pro Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity reaches 0.217 to 0.234, +0.098+0.098 to +0.115+0.115 over the constant letter (0.119), with every interval above zero, but SmolLM3-3B and Intern-S1-mini reach 0.378 and 0.542 with their best configurations, and THINK-512, which truncates, is level with or below the constant for both. On GSM8K Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity scores 0.068 to 0.070 in every configuration, which is +0.036+0.036 [+0.011+0.011, +0.063+0.063] over the oracle constant answer (0.034) in test and +0.011+0.011 [−0.027-0.027, +0.049+0.049], an interval containing zero, in replication, against 0.880 and 0.922 for the best configurations of the other two. The model that is best on the longevity letters is thus the weakest on MMLU-Pro and barely above a constant answer on GSM8K. We do not attribute this to fine-tuning, because the base model, Qwen3-1.7B, was not evaluated and the three models differ in size, training and thinking behaviour. Seeded sampling moves Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity’s letter accuracy by −0.013-0.013 to −0.018-0.018, only Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity parses LB-0038 reliably, and the tied-versus-untied comparison on FreeToken and the GEPA candidates are in Appendix B.

4.7 Sensitivity analyses

Each of the ten sensitivity analyses of the preregistration is descriptive. The strict scorer changes 2 of the 31 endpoint verdicts, and restricting to the never-called rows, which no earlier study had called, changes 3; these rows skew young and alive, with a mean LB-0030 age of 37.3 against 50.8 years and a share of LB-0042 rows whose follow-up says the participant was deceased of 0.022 against 0.346. That share counts a death at any time of the follow-up and is not the ten-year label, whose gold is “Yes” for a participant who died after ten years. The case study’s pool changes 1 and LB-0030 alone 2, and LB-0034 alone, LB-0042 alone, both role-break variants and the pooled partitions change none. Putting the left-out rows back changes no verdict of H1–H3 and 2 H4 claims (the skewed split in SmolLM3-3B and Intern-S1-mini).

5 Deviations and addenda

The preregistration allows a change only if it alters no request bytes, parsing, scoring or call order, and then only with a written note and a dry run that reproduces the recorded render hashes; any other change needs a new registration. After the freeze, the requests, the scoring and the primary criteria stayed as preregistered, with two exceptions that were not mechanical. We waived one stopping rule, once and for one stage: the check on Intern-S1-mini’s thinking switch had stopped the run that sends the reference answer, and we let that check record its failures and the run continue. And we settled one descriptive label after seeing the outputs: while auditing this paper we found that the two listed cases of the claim rule for the check sample are incomplete, so its general rule governs, and under it the claim for the skewed split in SmolLM3-3B fails where the narrower reading leaves it inconclusive (Section 4 gives both totals for H4).

Table 28 in Appendix C lists the deviations that bear on a result, and the appendix lists every exception, known deviation, pre-freeze decision and addendum with its date, reason, rule and the outputs seen at the time. No call touched a replication or test item before the freeze, and we saw only counts, and no accuracy, score or verdict of the main study, until every stage had run and the checkpoint’s record had been committed.

Everything computed after the outputs existed is labelled where it appears. This paper’s tables and figures only format aggregates committed in the authors’ repository, and its audit recomputes every verdict from its interval and agrees with the report on all of them (Appendix C).

6 Discussion and limitations

What the results say.

The gain of the thinking-off configuration over THINK-512 comes mostly from rows that THINK-512 left unparsed, so a search that starts from a configuration like this can find “repairs” that a thinking-off baseline already provides; GEPA, which searched prompt text only, repaired its broken starts, and none of its selected harnesses was more accurate than that baseline. Baseline adequacy still depends on the cell, because the rescue beat the thinking-off configuration by more than the margin on GSM8K for two models, so a thinking-off baseline is one to run and not one to assume adequate. Trivial baselines matter in both directions: only Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity beats the strongest constant label on the LongevityBench letters, and on GSM8K it is barely above a constant answer. Where prospective replication confirmed the distortion (6 of 15 evaluable pairs), the distortion was large and, within five points, the same on the check sample as on the selection sample. Some systematic distortions therefore persist across samples, and a replication run through the same pipeline reproduces them instead of revealing them. In the other pairs the claim fails (a descriptive label) or is inconclusive, and a defect whose claim fails need not be harmless. The checks that exposed the defects read inputs and scoring; their detections here are largely true by construction, and their false alarms (IR4, SCF1, SCF2, TB2) show that their thresholds need care.

Limitations.

The study covers three small models, three pools and six defects chosen from one line of work, so H4 says how replication behaves for these defects and not for the space of defects. “Prospective” has limits: earlier work had called most LongevityBench rows with other configurations, callers and one model variant, and the rows the case study had held out are excluded. Power is mixed. The H2 endpoint of Intern-S1-mini on GSM8K was expected to be inconclusive and is not (an informal expectation, Appendix K), H4 has no planned power, and its error control covers “holds” only. The GEPA arm searched prompt text only, with one proposer and four runs, so its negative result is about that space. The extended scorer and the role-break rule were fixed after the pilot’s parse audit. Unparsed counts as wrong by rule, so accuracy mixes parsing and correctness, and an unparsed answer may hide a correct answer, a wrong one or none; the study measures differences between configurations as served and not what the models know. The batch-invariant server differs from the standard one call for call, and everything ran on one GPU instance. Our intervals resample participant components (items in the two general pools) at a frozen harness, zero temperature and fixed prompts, so they cover item sampling and not prompt or judge variance (Messing, 2026). The freeze guards the rules and not model-specific tuning, which a preregistration for the next model would (Thomas et al., 2026). Zero temperature may turn some thinking into repetition; for the two models with a seeded arm substantial truncation persists under sampling (Section 4), and for SmolLM3-3B it is untested. The authors used Claude (Claude Code and claude.ai) and Codex for code, drafting and review, and they verified all analyses and claims.

Broader impact.

This paper contributes methodology for evaluating harness search and the pipelines that report it: a preregistered design, audit checks and a record of what each result rests on. It builds no new capability, since the models and benchmarks are public and the benchmark behind the longevity tasks derives from public survey data. The accuracies are those of small models on research tasks and do not support any use of these models for medical advice or clinical decisions. One misreading to avoid is that a thinking-off baseline is always enough, and the study shows two cells in which it is not.

7 Conclusion

In a design fixed in advance, most of the gain of a thinking-off configuration over a capped thinking configuration came from rows the capped configuration left unparsed, and the thinking-off configuration was non-inferior to the rescue and to four GEPA-selected harnesses in 11 of 13 endpoints, though not on GSM8K for two models. In 6 of the 15 evaluable (defect, model) pairs, the defect’s distortion of the reported number was larger than five points on the selection sample and reappeared, within five points, on the check sample. Reporting truncated and non-committed answers apart, running a thinking-off baseline and constant-label baselines, reading the rendered inputs and reconciling prompt tokens per call cost little, and they exposed the defects here.

Code and data availability

The study’s repository is not public at present. The paths, commits, tags and SHA256 values that this paper names belong to files in the authors’ repository, and we keep them so that a later public export can be checked against them (Appendix E). The run logs hold benchmark item text and model outputs and will not be released.

This arXiv version carries three ancillary files and a short README that describes them. The frozen preregistration and the aggregate analysis report are attached byte for byte. The addenda file is attached as it stood at the posting, with the row keys of five rows withheld because a row key identifies a benchmark row. The freeze time is recorded only in the authors’ private repository, in the hash file that the freeze commit adds, and it is not independently timestamped. The SHA256 of the frozen file (Appendix E) therefore lets a reader check that the ancillary copy is the file that was frozen, but not when it was frozen. A filtered public export of the rest is planned and will be linked in a later version of this paper: the code and its tests and the hash manifests, with no item-level or row-level content derived from the held-out rows.

The benchmarks and models are used under the terms their sources give, read on 2026-10-03. LongevityBench (dataset card insilicomedicine/longebench) is released under CC-BY-NC-4.0; its card states that the underlying source datasets (NHANES, GTEx, GEO, Olink, OpenGenes, SynergyAge) retain their original licences and access conditions, with which users must comply. MMLU-Pro (TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro) and GSM8K (openai/gsm8k) are under the MIT licence. Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity (insilicomedicine/Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity) is released under CC-BY-ND-4.0, and its base model Qwen3-1.7B is distributed under Apache-2.0; SmolLM3-3B (HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B) and Intern-S1-mini (internlm/Intern-S1-mini) are under Apache-2.0. The study uses the weights unmodified and redistributes neither benchmark item text nor model weights.

Appendix A Background: the case study this study follows

The case study.

The earlier study (v0.5 in the project’s records) ran a harness search around a frozen Qwen3-1.7B longevity model, served in its tied variant by FreeToken (Yang et al., 2026b). The search started from a parent configuration, CFG-THINK-64-ORIG (thinking on, 64 tokens for thinking and answer), and, driven by its failures on one shard, produced B1, a conditional rescue: when the first call used nearly all of its tokens, call again with a no-think suffix. B1’s gain in parse rate replicated on a second shard. A later audit found a simpler comparator, thinking disabled, that was as accurate as B1; it then found that the project’s caller had sent each benchmark row’s reference answer to the model as a prior assistant turn in every historical call that could be checked. Prompt-token reconciliation, the server’s prompt-token count against the local count of the intended request, was the evidence: the counts differed by the length of the reference turn.

The corrected re-evaluation.

After the caller was corrected, a preregistration was frozen (26 September 2026, 23:52:06 UTC) and run once on 556 holdout rows that no earlier experiment had called, though the comparator configurations had been defined after another line of experiments had called other holdout rows, among them 216 with a request equivalent to the no-think suffix. The parent parsed none of the 556 rows, so the preregistered reliability endpoint was nearly guaranteed. Thinking disabled was non-inferior to B1 at a margin of 0.10 (difference +0.012+0.012, interval [−0.028-0.028, +0.052+0.052]) at 47% of B1’s token cost; since every B1 first call reached the rescue threshold, B1 reduced to always adding the suffix. Post hoc, on LB-0030 no configuration clearly exceeded a constant guess of the age band most common in the two shards (band 30–45, accuracy 0.493, against 0.471 to 0.493 for the configurations). The case study’s conclusion was that prospective replication controlled selection noise but detected neither the inadequate comparator nor the evaluation defect, and that trivial baselines, input audits and prompt-token reconciliation did.

Why this study is not a replication of it.

The stack (vLLM in batch-invariant mode, not FreeToken), the model variant (untied output layer), two of the three models, two of the three pools and five of the six configurations are new, and the rules were fixed in advance for all of them. It is not blind to direction: the pilot showed that the parent truncates where the budget is small, and the preregistration says so (Section 3).

B.4 Trivial baselines, computed after the outputs existed

Chance is the mean of 1/k1/k over the rows (kk options). A constant letter or a constant label is the same answer on every row; the non-oracle constant is the most common gold letter or label of the other partition, the oracle constant the most common one of the partition itself (ties to the smallest). On LB-0030 and LB-0042 the order of the options is shuffled from row to row, so a constant letter cannot exploit an uneven label distribution and a constant label can. The strongest baseline of a task is the larger of its two oracle constants; the pool’s values are row-weighted means. For MMLU-Pro and GSM8K (addendum A12) the constants are a letter and an answer (the most common gold answer of the other partition, and of the partition itself); the strongest baseline is the oracle constant, and a free-form number has no chance level. Cells give accuracy and, in parentheses, the paired difference to the strongest oracle baseline; intervals for the pool are in Table 6, the rest in the files of the authors’ repository (Appendix E).

Appendix C Deviations, exceptions and addenda in full

In the authors’ repository (Appendix E) the frozen preregistration (docs/icml_ext/PREREG_ICML_EXT.md) records exceptions and known deviations before the freeze, together with its decisions of the days before it. After the freeze, departures are appended to docs/icml_ext/PREREG_ICML_EXT_ADDENDA.md, one entry each, under its section on deviation rules. This appendix lists them all: Table 28 gives the deviations that bear on a result, and the sections below give every exception, known deviation, pre-freeze decision and addendum. “Seen” states what had been seen of the study’s outputs when an entry was made.

C.1 Exceptions accepted before the freeze (X1–X9)

  • X1

    Three RECORD entries of the vLLM virtual environment do not match their files (two PyNvVideoCodec libraries and build_backend.py); they date from the original installation, not from the clone. Decided 2026-09-28.

  • X2

    FreeToken 0.1.3 opens a process-group store on its serving port plus one that PyTorch binds off loopback; it carries no model traffic. The runner allows exactly this one listener, on FreeToken only, while no connection to it comes from off the machine. The case study’s FreeToken runs very likely had it too.

  • X3

    FREETOKEN_ALLOW_CUDA_MISMATCH, the case study’s variable, is exempt from the credential-name check although its name contains “token”.

  • X4

    VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 in every vLLM run, because FlashInfer’s sampling kernel could not compile against the image’s CUDA toolkit.

  • X5

    A change of instance on 2026-09-28: the source instance’s GPU was no longer available, so the instance was cloned to one of the same configuration; the GPU identifier changed and the clone was verified against the recorded freeze, wheel, record and model hashes.

  • X6

    A restart of the container at 2026-09-29 00:57:25 UTC, which we did not initiate; no server was running, and the GPU identifier and the SSH settings were unchanged.

  • X7

    The first gate check (G1) ran on the checkpoint’s own directory, whose configuration declares tied embeddings, before the output-layer decision; its results were operational only.

  • X8

    AI-assisted readings and uploads (item-exposure contacts 1 and 2); the reading of the main export (contact 3) and the copy of the item files to the project’s own instance (contact 4) are in Appendix F.

  • X9

    A change of the physical GPU after a restart (addenda A1, A2).

C.2 Known deviations from the plans (K1–K9)

  • K1

    Three models instead of four; the FreeToken continuity on Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity only.

  • K2

    GEPA with a local proposer replaces Meta-Harness, so the proposer through an API and its budget fall away.

  • K3

  • K5

  • K6

  • K7

  • K8

C.3 Decisions between the first draft and the freeze

We revised the draft after our decisions on its first version, after a review in claude.ai, after two reviews and a final check in Codex (each given the file and not the authors’ repository), after our decisions on the summary of the drafting session, and after the reading of the rendered requests. Table 28 calls these decisions “Before the freeze”. The decisions that shape the endpoints were these:

  • •

    The primary set of H1 changed twice, first after the pilot’s parse rates and parsed answers were seen (no accuracy was used) and then after the first review in Codex, with THINK-64 against AUTHORS-1500 moved out to nine sanity checks.

  • •

    The scoring defect B was split into B1 and B2.

  • •

    The tied-output-layer defect E was redesigned so that the confirmatory instance serves the tied variant on both samples.

  • •

    One evaluability rule applies to every defect, and the family of H4 is fixed at 16 whatever is evaluable.

  • •

    The margin and the minimal difference are 0.05, with Bonferroni within each family.

After the reading, seven replication rows whose reference answers could be recovered from render-hash lists uploaded by mistake were flagged and left out of every analysis (the reading itself, item-exposure contact 3, concluded pass); Table 28 calls this “Rows left out”. The exclusion came after the last review in Codex and was not reviewed there.

C.4 Addenda after the freeze (A1–A12)

A1, A2 (2026-09-30)

A change of GPU. After we restarted the instance, the platform had assigned a different physical GPU of the same model. By the preregistration’s rules the work stopped before any copy or call. Every check passed on the new GPU; the determinism check (G2 (b)) was rerun on the pilot rows and passed for all three models, and its outputs equal the old GPU’s token for token. 9.33 GPU-hours, outside the budget; the new identifier is pinned. Seen: pilot rows only.

A3 (2026-09-30)

Two script stops. The chain script stopped twice during the GEPA search, both times from a fault in the script (a password check that failed under a shell option; a step that required an empty GPU while the task server stayed up). No run, call or check was affected. Seen: nothing of replication or test.

A4, A5 (2026-10-01, 2026-10-02)

The thinking-switch check. The defect-A pass of Intern-S1-mini stopped itself at gate (b): five of its first thinking-off calls (AUTHORS-1500) were not clean (cut at the limit with a think block opened and not closed). The gate held on all 3,849 thinking-off calls of the clean runs up to then. The preregistration had not foreseen that the injected defect could trigger the gate. We decided that in that stage only the gate records instead of stopping (commit aae8b11, runner a9478cee), that the idle server stops and its hours are counted (about 6.46 of its server-hours were idle), that the partial folder is moved out of the run root, and that the run is repeated from scratch under a new name. The repeat reproduced all 3,700 calls of the failed attempt token for token and failed the gate on 324 of the pass’s 1,204 thinking-off calls (the gate reads the completion, and all 1,204 prompts carry think tags that the chat template writes around the reference turn). By the repair rules this is confirmatory: the failed attempt is kept and reported, and only the repeat enters the analysis. Seen: counts only.

A6 (2026-10-02)

The checkpoint. It ran on the instance, since the local machine lacked memory. All 17 replication runs were complete with matching manifests; the derived rescue equals the real two-call sequence on 300 of 300 verification items per model; 15 of 16 pairs are evaluable; and the selections of the pipelines whose selection sample lies in replication were locked in a record (f033f23f) whose hash was committed before the first test call. Seen: counts, bounds and the record’s hash.

A7 (2026-10-02, 2026-10-03)

The determinism recheck. The test partition ran 14 runs and 267,056 calls, with no retry and no stop, and the recheck of 600 calls per model was identical on all three; the study used 54.53 of the 77 GPU-hours of the cost bound. Seen: counts.

A8 (2026-10-03)

The analysis environment. The preregistered analysis ran once on the instance (numpy 2.3.5, not the local 2.2.6; the resampling stream was checked equal for three seeds) after every pinned file matched its frozen hash, and the selections it reports equal the locked ones on all 24 comparisons. The code that computes three descriptive items the pinned driver lacks (tied versus untied, GEPA candidates, serving counts) was written after the outputs existed and is labelled so. Seen: all aggregates, for the first time.

A9 (2026-10-03)

Computed after the outputs. We shut the instance down and do not release it; the report and its tables were committed as aggregates (49e5f9c); the never-called rows’ composition (543 rows, 310 on the letter tasks) and constant-letter baselines were computed after the outputs existed.

A10 (2026-10-03)

Computed after the outputs. Constant-label baselines, because a constant letter is a weak floor where the option order is shuffled: the strongest baseline of the pool is 0.539 on test against 0.389 for the oracle constant letter. The strongest baseline is the one used in this paper.

A11 (2026-10-03)

The claim rule. The rule for DRD_{R} in the claim of H4. The audit of this paper recomputes the claim from its three adjusted intervals; the two sub-cases that the preregistration lists after its general rule were incomplete, the general rule governs, and the pinned code implements it (our decision). No verdict changes. Seen: all aggregates. Details below.

A12 (2026-10-03)

Computed after the outputs. The trivial baselines of MMLU-Pro (chance and the constant letter) and GSM8K (the constant answer), chosen on the other partition and oracle, next to every model’s accuracy in every grid configuration (holdout contact #57). Seen: aggregates, no item key or text.

C.5 The rule for DRD_{R} (addendum A11)

For DRD_{R} the preregistration says that it fails if its interval lies “wholly on the other side of its boundary” and lists two sub-cases, wholly within the band and wholly outside it with the opposite sign. The pinned code (scripts/icml_ext/analysis_h4.py, claim_verdict) implements the general phrase: DRD_{R} is graded in the direction of DSD_{S}’s sign, holds if it lies wholly beyond the band there, and fails if its interval lies wholly on the other side of that one boundary, which also covers an interval partly within the band and partly beyond its far edge. The general rule governs and the two sub-cases were incomplete. It matters for one pair, C in SmolLM3-3B: DS=−0.001D_{S}=-0.001 points down, so DRD_{R} would have to lie below −0.05-0.05, and its adjusted interval [−0.048-0.048, +0.063+0.063] lies wholly above it, so the claim cannot hold and is fails, a descriptive label. Read as the two sub-cases only, the claim would be inconclusive, and H4 would count 6 holds, 3 fails and 6 inconclusive instead of 6, 4 and 5; every other claim has the same verdict under both readings.

C.6 What this paper adds

This paper’s text, tables and figures format aggregates committed in the authors’ repository and add no computation except the counts of its own tables (verdict counts by family, the largest and smallest of a column) and the independent recomputation of every verdict from its interval, which agrees with the report on every endpoint that has a verdict (Appendix E).

Appendix D Expected in advance against observed

The preregistration states what it expected for several endpoints, from the pilot’s parse and truncation rates and parsed answers (never from accuracy). Table 29 sets each expectation next to what was observed. The directions of H1 and H3 were visible in the pilot, and the preregistration says so; this table shows the places where the outcome differed from the expectation, which are as informative as the places where it did not. “Inconclusive” in the Expected column is an informal expectation read off planned power under assumed effects (Appendix K), not a prediction with a decision rule.

Every path, commit, tag and SHA256 value in this paper is that of a file in the authors’ repository, which is not public at present (see the statement on code and data availability after the Conclusion). They are kept so that the planned public export can be checked against them; a reader cannot open these files until the export is linked.

The frozen record.

In the authors’ repository the preregistration (docs/icml_ext/PREREG_ICML_EXT.md) was frozen at 06:53:11 UTC on 30 September 2026, in commit 7f645ae, whose parent carries the tag pre-icml-ext-freeze; the tag prereg-icml-ext-frozen marks the freeze. Its SHA256 is

dec5dc25fdd0074a973926767a7a7f378e3dbc06eaccbf976d6df6f84dd2f515

The file docs/icml_ext/PREREG_ICML_EXT.sha256 holds the hash and the time, and the addenda are in docs/icml_ext/PREREG_ICML_EXT_ADDENDA.md. The outputs.

The report of the preregistered analysis and its tables are committed as aggregates in the authors’ repository, in docs/icml_ext/ANALYSIS_20261003/: the report has SHA256 1447c936d52523a1494169f30af239c7d36ce7e79e81655a6a91016570c22e0b, the folder’s manifest 37d3268a980974af6ab414af65b8b2b1a5b3d6071632f8f1867ffc3d871a8403. The code.

The files of the authors’ repository that fix the analysis are pinned in the preregistration by SHA256: scripts/icml_ext/analysis_stats.py (e6a2c4dc), analysis_records.py (7507fd6c), analysis_h4.py (2f5a82e7), analysis_run.py (d92ebfe2), defects.py (a2ad7e2e), scoring.py (3bce48ef) and runner_checks.py (ec77476e), and the caller scripts/paper_review/messages_for_inference.py (cc8debc7). The runner changed once after the freeze (addendum A4, commit aae8b11). The environment is vLLM 0.30.0 with the packages listed in the setup log (docs/icml_ext/SERVER_SETUP_LOG.md); the analysis ran with numpy 2.3.5. vLLM pull request 41674 (merged 2026-05-15) fixed a thinking-token budget that was silently ignored (JasonKeyiL (2026), vLLM project); the version used contains the fix, and H3 shows the budget acting.

This paper’s numbers.

Every number of the text is a value macro (\V applied to a key) that tools/values.py registers with the file of the authors’ repository that it reads (at git HEAD, never the working tree) and the path inside it; tools/gen.py writes common/numbers.tex and the tables from that registry, and --check fails if a committed generated file would change. audit/number_audit.py then (i) re-reads every registered value with its own path reader and formatter, (ii) recomputes the verdict of every endpoint that has one (all but the unevaluable pair of the 47) from its interval with the preregistered rules and compares it with the report’s, (iii) fails on any number in the hand-written text that is not a macro or an identifier, (iv) checks every hash, path and tag named in the text against the authors’ repository, and (v) checks the plotted values of the figures (tools/make_figures.py). audit/CLAIM_AUDIT.md maps each claim of the text to its evidence.

Appendix F Exposure and disclosure

Every contact of the authors or their tools with held-out material is logged in the authors’ repository (docs/paper_review/HOLDOUT_EXPOSURE_LOG.md, numbered contacts; docs/icml_ext/ITEM_EXPOSURE_LOG.md, contacts with the extension’s items by outside services), and before it happens, with one exception that Table 30 marks. The case study’s holdout contacts are #1 to #38; those of this study are #39 to #58 and #60. Other later contacts, including the preparation of the ancillary files and the posting of this version, are logged in the repository and are not listed here. Item-exposure contacts 1 and 2 are uploads of the pilot’s reading export and runner and of a spot-check and the GEPA code to claude.ai; contact 3 is the AI-assisted reading of the main export (concluded pass; one of us relayed the reading and its conclusion and also checked the conclusion); contact 4 is the copy of the main item files to the project’s own GPU instance, which is not an outside service.

The mistaken upload (#47) and its consequence.

One of us uploaded the three render-hash lists to the claude.ai conversation of the reading, together with the export. A defect-A entry is the hash of a request that carries the row’s reference answer, so for a row whose clean request is known, the answer can be recovered by testing each candidate against the hash. Seven replication rows are both in the reading’s sample and among the defect-A rows, and we flagged them and left them out of every analysis, whether or not anyone tried. Nothing else in the replication or test partitions was disclosed this way. The reader’s statement, relayed by one of us and not checked independently, is that the reading did not open the lists and did not attempt a reconstruction.

Files derived from held-out rows.

This paper and the committed analysis report carry aggregates that include the rows flagged v21_holdout (the sensitivity analysis), so both are listed in docs/paper_review/HOLDOUT_DERIVED_FILES.md of the authors’ repository, and they hold no row index, key or content. The run logs, which hold item text, stay off the authors’ repository and will not be released. We drafted the paper with Claude Code and reviewed it in claude.ai and in Codex. Contact #58 is the copy given to Codex, which was the two files of the named preprint and not the repository, a run log or any item text, and contact #60 is the PDF reviewed in claude.ai. Any further upload of the draft is a new contact, logged first.

Appendix G Serving details

Servers.

The main study ran each model on a vLLM server started by a pinned script with these flags (the model directory, served name and chat-template file differ by model; Intern-S1-mini adds --trust-remote-code and a limit of zero images and videos):

vllm serve <model directory> --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
  --dtype bfloat16 --served-model-name <name>
  --chat-template <pinned file> --generation-config vllm
  --reasoning-parser qwen3
  --reasoning-config ’{"reasoning_start_str": "<think>",
                       "reasoning_end_str": "</think>"}’
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-chunked-prefill
  --max-model-len 4096

with the environment cleared to a fixed list of variables, among them VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 and VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 (exception X4). Every request sets thinking on or off explicitly, carries a seed (irrelevant at zero temperature) and asks for the token IDs and the rendered prompt; the runner compares both with its own render on every call and stops on a difference, except in the defect-A pass, where the reference answer makes them differ by design. Each stage runs its start checks before the first call and again after the last (no credential-like variable name, no connection off the machine, loopback-only listening, the model directory and the hash of its configuration, the template, the flags, and the render check against the pinned list), and a watcher samples the server’s connections from launch. The watchers flagged nothing on the vLLM servers; on each FreeToken server they flagged only the single listener of exception X2.

Cost.

The GEPA search used 6.63 GPU-hours, the replication partition 22.07 and the test partition 25.83, 54.53 of the 77 of the cost bound; the rerun of the determinism check on the new GPU (9.33 hours) is outside it.

Per-run counts.

Table 31 gives, per run and configuration, the calls, the disagreements between the server’s reasoning split and the local one (logged on every call and never a stop; in the pilot they all fell after a forced end of thinking, or where the limit cut a multibyte character, and were equal once the four tags were removed), the calls in which a start-of-turn marker re-opened a turn (role breaks, all in SmolLM3-3B’s BUDGET-512-1500), and mean tokens and seconds per call. The counts include every row called, flagged rows and LB-0038 among them.

Appendix H How the related work was searched

We searched arXiv, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, Hugging Face papers, GitHub and venue pages from 2024-01 to 2026-10-03, with topic queries only (no item content), starting from the seed papers and their references and citers, in six topic slices: harness and agent-system evaluation; optimisers and agent baselines; reasoning evaluation under token budgets; evaluation-pipeline defects; inference engines and checkpoint identity; preregistration and replication. The agents behind the slices made 1,006 web calls. A shared cap of 200 web searches ran out during the search, the arXiv and Semantic Scholar interfaces were rate-limited, and three of the six slices (reasoning evaluation, inference engines, pipeline defects) were stopped by a rate limit and resumed to write up what they had already read, without new searches. “We found no study that” therefore means that none was found, not that none exists, and most recent work on harness evolution is an unreviewed preprint.

Identifiers, titles, authors and dates of the cited papers were checked against arXiv. The statements in Section 2 about a paper’s design were checked against its text for the papers marked as read in the matrix in the authors’ repository (docs/icml_ext/RELATED_WORK_MATRIX.md), and otherwise rest on its abstract. For the GitHub pull requests cited, the merge date and the release that contains the merge commit were checked through the GitHub interface.

Appendix I H4 in detail

This appendix restates, from the frozen preregistration, what Section 3.4 summarises: the quantity each claim reports, how each defect is built and what it is compared with, the rows of its samples, the bound that decides whether its pair is evaluable, and the predicate and threshold of every check.

The reported quantity and the claim.

For an instance II (a defect and a model) and its clean counterpart KK, the reported quantity is the accuracy of a fixed configuration, the pipeline’s start ss, on the letter pool: aS=accS​(s)a_{S}=\mathrm{acc}_{S}(s) on the selection sample SS and aR=accR​(s)a_{R}=\mathrm{acc}_{R}(s) on the check sample RR. The start is THINK-1536 (for E, the case study’s CFG-THINK-1536-ORIG), and THINK-64 in the instance of D. No claim selects anything. Then DS=aS​(I)−aS​(K)D_{S}=a_{S}(I)-a_{S}(K), DR=aR​(I)−aR​(K)D_{R}=a_{R}(I)-a_{R}(K) and Γ=DR−DS\Gamma=D_{R}-D_{S}. The claim holds if the adjusted interval of DSD_{S} lies wholly outside ±m\pm m, that of DRD_{R} lies wholly outside ±m\pm m on the side of DSD_{S}’s point estimate, and that of Γ\Gamma lies within ±m\pm m. It fails if any of the three lies wholly on the other side of its boundary (DSD_{S}’s wholly within ±m\pm m; DRD_{R}’s wholly within ±m\pm m, or wholly outside it on the opposite side; Γ\Gamma’s wholly outside ±m\pm m), and it is inconclusive otherwise. Here m=0.05m=0.05 and the intervals have the adjusted level of the family of 16; an interval that fails decides the claim even if another is still open, and the error control covers “holds” only.

Defect D and the selection.

For D the reported quantity is the gain g=acc⁡(c∗)−acc⁡(s)g=\mathrm{acc}(c^{*})-\mathrm{acc}(s) of the selected configuration c∗c^{*} over the start, on SS and on RR. The selection picks c∗c^{*} as the most accurate member on SS of the search space (THINK-64, THINK-512, THINK-1536, RESCUE-1500 and BUDGET-512-1500; ties go to the earlier member), and AUTHORS-1500 lies outside it, so that it can act as the simple comparator that a search never considered. Because c∗c^{*} does not depend on the start, the instance of D and its counterpart select the same c∗c^{*} in every resample, the selection cancels, and DS=accS​(THINK-1536)−accS​(THINK-64)D_{S}=\mathrm{acc}_{S}(\text{\mbox{{\small THINK-1536}}})-\mathrm{acc}_{S}(\text{\mbox{{\small THINK-64}}}), with the same difference on RR for DRD_{R}. The selection itself, the gains it reports and every interval that follows a selection are descriptive and enter no claim.

Defects, comparators and samples.

Table 32 gives for each defect how it is built, the samples SS and RR, the clean counterpart it is compared with and how the two are resampled, and the bound of its pair. All samples leave out the flagged rows (Section 3). Where an instance and its counterpart share their rows, one resample of the units serves both, so DSD_{S} and DRD_{R} are paired; Γ\Gamma pairs the bb-th resample of SS with the bb-th of RR, drawn with their own seeds.

Evaluability.

A pair is evaluable if its bound exceeds mm (a bound of exactly mm does not). Otherwise it is reported as not evaluable, with its bound, makes no claim and is not counted as failing, and the family stays at 16. The bounds were computed from parse, gold-change and answer-difference indicators on the replication data at the checkpoint, before the first test call. For B1 the start must parse the same rows in the instance and its counterpart, and for B2 the gold must be the release’s in both; the analysis stops if not.

The checks and their rules.

Each check is evaluated on the records of an instance, and “fires” means that one of its rules holds. The rules and thresholds were fixed before the study; their outcomes are descriptive, and what is empirical is how often they fire on clean instances (Section 4). The rules of PR and every interval that follows a selection on SS are descriptive labels, not tests: the selection makes accS​(c∗)\mathrm{acc}_{S}(c^{*}) and the gain optimistic. Tables 33 and 34 give each rule’s predicate and threshold.

Appendix J The GEPA arm in detail

What GEPA searched.

GEPA version 0.1.4 (Agrawal et al., 2025) edited two text components and nothing else: the system prompt, which replaces the row’s system message (seed: the rows’ own system message; limit 3,800 characters), and an instruction appended to the user turn after a blank line (seed: empty; limit 3,000 characters). The request parameters (thinking on or off, the token limit, the temperature) belong to the start and were not searched. The clean start is the request of AUTHORS-1500 (thinking off, 1,500 tokens, zero temperature) and the broken start that of THINK-64; the seed harnesses are the grid’s own runs of those two configurations. The arm therefore searched prompt text only, and its negative result (no selected harness more accurate than the thinking-off baseline) is about that space: it says nothing about searching the thinking switch, the token limits or retry rules. The task model is Qwen3-1.7B-Longevity (untied) on the batch-invariant server. The proposer is Intern-S1-mini on the standard server at concurrency one, with thinking on, its card’s sampling values (temperature 0.8, top-pp 1.0, top-kk 50), at most 8,192 tokens and a seed per request. GEPA’s settings are its defaults except: a reflection minibatch of 3 rows; Pareto selection of candidates over instances; a round-robin choice of the component to edit; acceptance only on strict improvement; perfect-score minibatches skipped; no merging; no evaluation cache.

Rows and allocation.

The arm uses 300 rows of the search partition’s three letter tasks (120 of LB-0030, 60 of LB-0034 and 120 of LB-0042), drawn with seed 20261011 from search rows that are neither pilot rows nor rows the case study had held out; LB-0038 is left out because its score is an age error. They form a training set of 150 rows (60, 30 and 60 by task) and a validation set of 150 rows (the same split); the lists are the same in the four runs. A candidate scores one on a row when the primary scorer’s parsed answer equals the gold and zero otherwise, an unparsed answer included. The proposer sees a row’s user message, the task model’s output, reasoning and answer, and feedback (correct, incorrect, unparsed, or cut at the token limit); it never sees the gold or a replication or test row. The four runs are the clean and the broken start, each with GEPA seeds zero and one.

Checks on a candidate, and the copy rule.

Before any call a candidate is checked, and one that fails is recorded and scored zero without a call: each component is text within its limit; neither holds a chat-template control string; neither holds a run of 40 or more consecutive characters of a row’s user message that occurs in fewer than 10 of the arm’s rows (the copy rule: wording shared by many rows may be copied, a row’s own text may not); every render plus the token limit fits the 4,096-token context. The soft switches /think and /no_think were allowed and each candidate records whether it holds one; none of the selected harnesses does. A separate script re-checked the four selected texts against the arm’s rows and found no violation of the copy rule and no identifier or number sequence of an item.

Budget, selection and ties.

The budget is 6,000 metric calls per run (20 candidates on 300 rows). It is soft: GEPA checks it between iterations, so a run may end slightly above it, and the four runs used 6,003 to 6,147 calls. GEPA spends 6 metric calls per proposal, 150 on the seed’s validation evaluation and 150 on each accepted candidate. The selected harness of a run is its candidate with the highest mean validation score, ties going to the lowest candidate index; if no proposal was accepted it is the seed. The selected texts were recorded, with their SHA256, before the harness was run on any replication row. Each was then run on every letter row of the replication and test partitions, on the main server with its start’s request parameters.

The four selected harnesses.

The texts below are as selected, wrapped for display; a character outside ASCII is written [U+XXXX] ([U+2265] is the sign for greater than or equal, [U+03BC] the Greek letter mu, [U+00B2] a superscript two). Each candidate’s SHA256 is the one recorded before any replication call in the authors’ repository; the wrapping means that it cannot be recomputed from this page. A small language model generated the texts; we did not check their medical statements, and they must not be used as clinical guidance. Validation scores and accuracies are in Appendix B.
